function: MADDPG and P2P-VFRL agents jointly learn UAV trajectory, subchannel and transmit-power allocation, and CPU allocation in a UL-NOMA HAP-UAV network to minimize average AoI (pp. 7-8).
system: No RIS; HAP 20 km, 2 UAV-BSs 400 m, up to 40 users, UL multi-carrier NOMA, 10 MHz; UAV-HAP link 2.4 GHz; antennas unspecified (pp. 4, 9).
method: Online multi-agent actor-critic RL: MADDPG (centralized training) and peer-to-peer vertical federated RL (P2P-VFRL) with parameter averaging; reinforcement and federated paradigms (pp. 8-9).
data_channel: No dataset; custom simulator: distance-based gain beta0/d^2, Rayleigh fast fading, Gaussian CSI error, random user placement in 200 km x 200 km; trained online (pp. 4, 7, 9).
test_conditions: Trained online and evaluated in the same simulated scenario; sweeps of users (10-40), CPU, power, subchannels, task size, CSI uncertainty (0-20%); no unseen-condition test stated (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Baseline 1 (maximum power, no power allocation), Baseline 2 (whole task in one slot, fixed method) and MADDPG versus P2P-VFRL; no earlier learned method from literature (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Average AoI (time slots), reward (negative average AoI) over episodes, percentage AoI improvement, number of failed tasks, agent communication overhead (pp. 9-12).
complexity: Order O(N_agents*D*E_episode*(C_a+C_c)) for both approaches, MADDPG parameter-count order (35), and communication overhead N_agents versus N_agents(N_agents-1) (p. 9).
openness: Simulation code of both approaches released at https://dx.doi.org/10.21227/8yvb-e654, ref. [41] (pp. 10, 13).
q1_support: p. 4: "denotes the power gain of a channel with reference" (distance d0 = 1 m). The channel is a custom path-loss simulator with Rayleigh fast fading (Table II, p. 9) and a Gaussian CSI error (p. 7); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 7: "we adopt online learning". The paper never states that a trained model is tested on conditions not used for training; the sweeps of users, CPU, power, subchannels, task size and CSI uncertainty (pp. 10-12) are not reported as such tests, and the state size depends on M (p. 8).
q3_support: p. 9: "Algorithm 1: Online P2P-VFRL and MADDPG"; p. 12: "compared it with well-known algorithm of MADDPG". The comparisons are Baseline 1 (maximum power, p. 10), Baseline 2 (whole task, p. 11) and MADDPG versus P2P-VFRL, two modes of one algorithm; no earlier learned method or separate standard learner (DQN, DDPG) is a baseline.
q4_support: p. 9: "computational complexity of both approaches can be obtained" as O(N_agents*D*E_episode*(C_a+C_c)), eq. (36); the number of MADDPG parameters is given as an order in eq. (35).
q5_support: p. 10: "The source code for the simulation of both approaches are available in [41]." Ref. [41] on p. 13 gives the DOI "org/10.21227/8yvb-e654" (https://dx.doi.org/10.21227/8yvb-e654).
notes: Included as area 6: learned power and subchannel allocation for aerial links is a physical-layer decision (actions, pp. 7-8) learned jointly with UAV trajectory and CPU allocation, so the above_phy rule for aerial links lets it pass. The objective is the AoI of offloaded computing tasks. q3 judgement: MADDPG and P2P-VFRL are both presented as proposed (abstract, p. 1) and are two modes of one Algorithm 1 with an FRL-mode flag (p. 9), so MADDPG is treated as a variant of the proposed method, not an earlier baseline; if the reviewer counts MADDPG as a standard-algorithm baseline, q3 would change to 1. Table II (p. 9) and Fig. 6 (p. 11) were read from the page images.
